FeetFinder Taxes

The shop does not set money aside for the IRS. If you sell, the return is yours, including the months that felt too small to count.

Dark-Ero editorialUpdated 2026-11-1018+

At a glance

FeetFinder's seller agreement says taxes are solely the seller's responsibility.

The IRS expects gig income reported even when no 1099 arrives.

Self-employment tax is 15.3 percent once net earnings from self-employment reach $400.

Key takeaways

  • US sellers submit a W-9 at registration, and sellers outside the US submit a W-8BEN.
  • FeetFinder's FAQ says US sellers over $600 a year get 1099 forms from Segpay, which is the shop's own rule.
  • The federal 1099-K bar for marketplaces is over $20,000 and more than 200 transactions.
  • For 2026 payments, the 1099-NEC threshold rose to $2,000.
  • This page is US federal information for adults, not a filing you should copy blind.

Yes, FeetFinder income is taxable in the United States. The seller agreement says taxes are solely the seller's responsibility, and the IRS says gig income is reported even when nobody sends a form.

The long version, with the form table, is FeetFinder taxes. Tax rules change, and a CPA or an enrolled agent is the person who should see your return.

This note is US federal information checked against public IRS pages and the shop's own agreement in October 2026. It is not tax advice, and it is not your state's form.

Disclosure: Dark-Ero is independent, with no affiliate link on this page. Adults 18+ only.

You report it anyway

Money from feet pics, clips or worn items is taxable whether the work is a side month or a full calendar. The IRS says all income is taxable unless the tax law says it is not, including cash and amounts under any form threshold.

Most active sellers belong on Schedule C, which is the form for an activity you run for profit with continuity. Hobby income is still reported, and hobby expenses are the ones the IRS limits, so the label is not a way to skip the return.

The seller agreement lets FeetFinder file reports with the IRS, withhold where US tax law requires it, and close an account over tax non-compliance. You also state that you will report the payments where you live.

The agreement says the company is not responsible for withholding income, payroll or Social Security tax for you. You are not an employee, and nothing is parked for April unless you park it.

Which 1099 might show up

FeetFinder's FAQ says US sellers who make over $600 a year receive 1099 forms from Segpay, and that the forms are discreet. The FAQ does not name which 1099, and that $600 figure is the shop's policy, not the federal bar.

For payment apps and online marketplaces, the federal 1099-K threshold is over $20,000 and more than 200 transactions. The IRS said the One Big Beautiful Bill restored that older bar, and a state can still use a lower one.

For payments made in 2026, the 1099-NEC threshold, and the 1099-MISC threshold for rents, prizes and other income, rose from $600 to $2,000. A missing form does not erase the income, and a wrong form is corrected by the issuer, not by the IRS rewriting it for you.

US sellers hand over a W-9 so the payer has a taxpayer identification number. A wrong number can trigger backup withholding at 24 percent, which is a paperwork problem you can avoid at signup.

Schedule C and self-employment tax

Most US sellers put the gross receipts on Schedule C, subtract ordinary business costs, and figure self-employment tax on Schedule SE when net earnings reach $400. The 1099 gross amount is not already reduced for fees or refunds, so your own ledger is the starting point.

The self-employment rate is 15.3 percent, made of 12.4 percent for Social Security and 2.9 percent for Medicare, applied to 92.35 percent of net profit. You can deduct half of that self-employment tax when you figure adjusted gross income, and the Social Security slice stops at an annual wage cap.

A simplified illustration in the source material, a single filer in the 12 percent bracket with $6,000 of gross sales, landed near $1,192 of extra federal tax after the Basic fee and the plan. That is about a quarter of the net in that sketch, and your bracket, your state and your deductions will move it.

Ordinary and necessary costs can include the seller plan, the service fee, props used for the shoots, and a slice of a home office that meets the regular-and-exclusive test. Personal living costs stay off the schedule.

If you expect to owe $1,000 or more at filing and withholding will not cover the safe harbor, estimated payments are the usual answer. For the 2026 tax year the remaining date people still trip over is 15 January 2027, which you can skip by filing and paying in full by 1 February 2027.

What to set aside

There is no single IRS percentage for this work. A practical habit is to move a slice of every payout into a separate account, using your own bracket rather than a stranger's screenshot.

Sellers outside the United States follow their own country's rules, and FeetFinder asks them for a W-8BEN rather than a W-9. Britain is covered in our how to sell feet pics in the UK page.

The HMRC version on the ranking site is how to sell feet pics in the UK. The trading allowance is the figure people misread as a feet-pic exemption.

Australia is a third system, in our sell feet pics in Australia note. A US form does not satisfy the ATO.

The Australian source page is sell feet pics in Australia. Do not file a US Schedule C from Sydney because a blog mentioned one.

Whether the sale is lawful is a different question from whether it is taxable. The US legal map is is selling feet pics legal.

Our is selling feet pics legal page is the shorter cut. Lawful sales are still income.

The shops, if you are still choosing where the income will come from, are under feet marketplaces. Keep a spreadsheet from the first sale, with the date, the gross and the fee.

Verdict

Report the income, keep the receipts, and expect self-employment tax once the net crosses $400. A 1099 is a copy of a number, not the thing that creates the tax.

Set cash aside from each payout and ask a professional before you file if the year got complicated. This is general information for adults, not a return.

FAQ

Do I pay tax on FeetFinder earnings?

Yes, US sellers report the income even when it is part-time and even when no 1099 arrives. The seller agreement also puts the tax on you.

What if I made less than $600?

You still report it, because the IRS taxes the income rather than the form. Self-employment tax applies once net earnings from self-employment reach $400.

Will I get a 1099?

FeetFinder's FAQ says US sellers over $600 a year get forms from Segpay, and that $600 rule is the shop's, not the federal 1099-K bar. You report the money either way.

What is the 1099-K threshold?

For marketplaces, the federal bar is over $20,000 and more than 200 transactions in the year. Your state may require a form at a lower amount.

How do I report the income?

Most US sellers use Schedule C for the gross and the expenses, then Schedule SE if net self-employment earnings are $400 or more. The totals carry to Form 1040.

Does FeetFinder withhold tax from payouts?

Normally no, so plan to pay the bill yourself. Backup withholding at 24 percent can apply if the taxpayer number on the W-9 is wrong.
